# Source packages {.dark-slide background-color="#111C26"}

[BLOCK 5 &middot; PART A]{.eyebrow}

[Downloading, inspecting, building, and installing a source package.]{.subhead}

## New container

::: {.demo-label}
Live
:::

```bash
exit                                          # leave the old container
docker run --rm -it --name rlab rocker/r-base bash
apt-get update && apt-get install -y libxml2-dev
R -q
```

From here on we do each step by hand: download, inspect, build, check,
install.

## `download.packages()`

```r
options(repos = c(CRAN = "https://cloud.r-project.org"))
dir.create("/tmp/dl")

download.packages(c("xml2", "R6"), destdir = "/tmp/dl", type = "source")
```

```text
trying URL 'https://cloud.r-project.org/src/contrib/xml2_1.6.0.tar.gz'
trying URL 'https://cloud.r-project.org/src/contrib/R6_2.6.1.tar.gz'
     [,1]   [,2]
[1,] "xml2" "/tmp/dl/xml2_1.6.0.tar.gz"
[2,] "R6"   "/tmp/dl/R6_2.6.1.tar.gz"
```

It returns a two-column matrix of names and file paths, for the packages
that downloaded successfully
([`?download.packages`](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/utils/html/download.packages.html)).
Keep it as the record of what you got.

## `download.packages()` does not resolve dependencies

**You get exactly the packages you named.** Combine it with
`tools::package_dependencies()` for a full set. The local-repository
section does this.

**`type =` decides what you get.** `"source"` gets the tarball; `"binary"`
gets the platform binary if the repository has one.

**It downloads from `repos`.** Point `repos` at a dated snapshot and you get
the same files every time.

## What is in the tarball

```bash
cd /tmp/dl
tar tzf xml2_1.6.0.tar.gz | cut -d/ -f2 | sort -u
```

```text
build       DESCRIPTION  inst     MD5       README.md  tests     vignettes
cleanup     configure    LICENSE  man       R          tools
configure.win            NAMESPACE          NEWS.md    src
```

| Entry | Role |
|---|---|
| `DESCRIPTION`, `NAMESPACE` | Metadata; what is imported and exported |
| `R/` | R source, unlike the installed form |
| `src/` | C/C++/Fortran source |
| `configure` | Run by `R CMD INSTALL` before anything else |
| `cleanup` | Run by `R CMD build`, and by `R CMD INSTALL --clean` |
| `man/`, `vignettes/`, `tests/` | Docs and tests |
| `inst/` | Copied recursively into the installed package |
| `build/` | Written by `R CMD build` |

See [Package structure](https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-exts.html#Package-structure)
in Writing R Extensions.

## The CRAN tarball is already built

```bash
tar tzf xml2_1.6.0.tar.gz | grep -E 'build/|MD5|inst/doc'
```

```text
xml2/MD5
xml2/inst/doc/modification.R
xml2/inst/doc/modification.html
xml2/inst/doc/modification.Rmd
xml2/build/vignette.rds
xml2/build/partial.rdb
```

```bash
tar xzOf xml2_1.6.0.tar.gz xml2/MD5 | head -3
```

```text
86de947ee4775f56c846e6f74e6cc970 *DESCRIPTION
41a6ad86ba30307f1996d7c5f7ff04c1 *LICENSE
5fd50f3190fd7b2ddc811a7cfa1fafb3 *NAMESPACE
```

::: {.note}
[CRAN tarballs are built]{.note-label}
A CRAN tarball is the output of `R CMD build`, not a git checkout.
`build/` and the rendered vignettes in `inst/doc/` were added by the build.
`MD5` is only written with `R CMD build --md5`
([build.R](https://github.com/wch/r-source/blob/trunk/src/library/tools/R/build.R)).
:::

## `R CMD build`: directory to tarball

::: {.demo-label}
Live
:::

```bash
tar xzf xml2_1.6.0.tar.gz
R CMD build xml2
```

```text
* checking for file 'xml2/DESCRIPTION' ... OK
* preparing 'xml2':
* checking DESCRIPTION meta-information ... OK
* cleaning src
* running 'cleanup'
* installing the package (it is needed to process help pages)
* saving partial Rd database
* creating vignettes ... OK
* cleaning src
* checking for LF line-endings in source and make files and shell scripts
* checking for empty or unneeded directories
* building 'xml2_1.6.0.tar.gz'
```

## What `R CMD build` does

- **Installs the package** into a temporary library, to rebuild vignettes
  and to run `\Sexpr` macros in the help pages.
- **Rebuilds vignettes**, which runs their code. The packages the vignettes
  need must be installed.
- **Cleans up**: runs `cleanup`, converts line endings in `src/`, and leaves
  out files matching `.Rbuildignore`.

See [Building package tarballs](https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-exts.html#Building-package-tarballs)
in Writing R Extensions. Other flags: `--no-manual`, `--resave-data`,
`--compact-vignettes`, `--md5` (`R CMD build --help`).

## `--no-build-vignettes`

Rebuilding a tarball that already has vignettes replaces the shipped ones,
and warns:

```text
Warning: 'inst/doc' files
    'modification.Rmd', 'modification.html', 'modification.R'
  ignored as vignettes have been rebuilt.
  Run R CMD build with --no-build-vignettes to prevent rebuilding.
```

With the flag, the shipped vignettes are kept:

```bash
R CMD build --no-build-vignettes xml2
```

::: {.note}
[When you need `R CMD build`]{.note-label}
For CRAN tarballs you usually do not: they are already built. You need it
for your own packages, to turn a git checkout into a tarball for a
repository.
:::

## `build` vs `INSTALL` vs `check`

| Command | Input | Output | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `R CMD build` | Source **directory** | `pkg_1.2.3.tar.gz` | Make a distributable tarball |
| `R CMD INSTALL` | Tarball **or** directory | Package in a library | Make it usable |
| `R CMD check` | Tarball (recommended) | `pkg.Rcheck/` | Test the package |

```bash
R CMD INSTALL --library=/usr/local/lib/R/site-library xml2_1.6.0.tar.gz
```

Useful `INSTALL` flags (`R CMD INSTALL --help`): `--build` (also produce a
binary), `--no-test-load`, `--configure-args=`, `--configure-vars=`,
`--libs-only`.

## Installing a local tarball

```r
install.packages("/tmp/dl/xml2_1.6.0.tar.gz", repos = NULL, type = "source")
```

```r
# several tarballs in one call
install.packages(Sys.glob("/tmp/dl/*.tar.gz"), repos = NULL, type = "source")
```

::: {.note}
[`repos = NULL`]{.note-label}
For a single `.tar.gz` path, `install.packages()` infers `repos = NULL`
if you do not pass `repos`. For several files, set it yourself. With
`repos = NULL`, dependencies are not resolved, so install them first
([`?install.packages`](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/utils/html/install.packages.html)).
:::

## A repository resolves the install order

```r
install.packages("xml2", repos = "file:///opt/pkgrepo")
```

With a `PACKAGES` index next to the tarballs, `install.packages()` resolves
dependencies and order itself. We build that repository in the last
section. First, checking.
